- Increasing learning rate to 0.001 will help the model converge faster and potentially achieve better performance
- The validation metrics being better than training metrics indicates the model has capacity to learn more from the data
- With Adam optimizer and cross-entropy loss, a slightly higher learning rate is safe and often beneficial
- The current transforms (random_crop, random_flip, normalize) provide good regularization, allowing for more aggressive learning
- No class weighting changes needed as precision and recall are well-balanced across metrics

This change should help close the performance gap and improve overall accuracy while maintaining the good regularization provided by the current data augmentation strategy.
